newsitem.title: UK: Punt slide shows ERM rates are key for EMU.
newsitem.headline: Punt slide shows ERM rates are key for EMU.

text.p: The Irish pound's sharp slide on Wednesday is one of the clearest signals yet that markets believe currencies starting European monetary union will be fixed at their central rates in the European exchange rate mechanism (ERM), analysts said.

Since the beginning of 1997 the punt had been trading more than 10 percent above its ERM midrate against the core bloc of EMU candidates, hauled up by its soaring neighbour sterling and an attractive interest rate premium over the German mark.

However, as markets have grown more and more confident that ERM central rates will be the eventual conversion rates for EMU and that Ireland will be part of the single currency in 1999, the punt's position has became a complete anomaly.
Even in the wake of Wednesday's slide of more than three percent against the mark, the punt at 2.5880 marks is still more than 17 pfennigs above its ERM parity of 2.4111.

"Markets have been given clear signals from EU officials both that EMU will start at the beginning of 1999 and that ERM central rates are very likely to be the conversion rates," said Jesper Dannesboe, economist at ABN AMRO.
"If Ireland is to be included as an EMU member in the first wave of the project then the current pattern of market prices and yields is significantly at odds with these objectives."

Crucially, the magnetic pull of sterling, which has been fuelled by similar economic cycles in the UK and Ireland and a high bilateral trade relationship, is waning as long as Britain remains undecided on EMU, say analysts.
Wednesday's drop of more than two percent against sterling highlights this, traders said.

"What's clear is that faced with a choice of trading on the Irish government's EMU desire or the vestiges of its old UK relationship, the market is beginning to plump for the former," said Paul Meggyesi, senior currency economist at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
"The key issue now is where the market believes the EMU conversion rate will be, and if they are going for the ERM central rates then the punt has further to go."
All other aspiring EMU entrants have already gravitated to near their ERM central rates, including EMU "hopefuls" like the Italian lira which is hovering around 990 per mark.
The punt has stuck out like a sore thumb as a result and market arbitrageurs sensed a killing.

"The sheer scope of the potential drop from over 2.60 marks to the central rate about 2.41 is just too big a hole to leave unfilled," said one trader at a major U.S. trading house here. Pressure on the punt began building after April 15 when Irish finance minister Ruairi Quinn said he was somewhat concerned with the punt's strength in the ERM and would prefer if it were closer to its ERM mid-point.
Traders said central bank intervention to buoy the punt over the past couple of weeks was not sustainable.

"The central bank was not prepared to see a sharp depletion of its reserves and seems to have signalled yesterday that the punt should find its own level," said Brian Martin, chief economist, forex at BZW.
